stimuli.text: Researchers collected data from 300 fifth-grade students. For each one, they recorded working memory span and reading comprehension score. The correlation between the two measures was r = +0.52.

Researchers collected data from 600 university students. For each one, they recorded conscientiousness score on a personality inventory and grade point average. The correlation between the two measures was r = +0.35.

Researchers investigated whether the presence of other people slows the reporting of an emergency. They recruited 80 university students and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition were filling in a form in a room with four other people when smoke began to enter the room. Participants in the other condition were filling in the form alone when smoke began to enter the room. The researchers then recorded the time in seconds before each participant left the room to report the smoke.

Researchers investigated whether a night without sleep slows reaction time. They recruited 60 adult volunteers and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition stayed awake all night in the laboratory. Participants in the other condition slept for eight hours in the laboratory. The researchers then recorded the average time in milliseconds that each participant took to press a button when a light appeared.

Researchers collected data from 1,000 students. For each one, they recorded intelligence test score at age 11 and average school grade at age 16. The correlation between the two measures was r = +0.60.

Researchers investigated whether guided hints help children learn to solve puzzles. They recruited 64 five-year-old children and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Children in one condition solved practice puzzles with hints from an adult that were gradually reduced. Children in the other condition solved the same practice puzzles alone. The researchers then recorded the number of new puzzles out of ten that each child later solved without help.

Researchers investigated whether keeping a gratitude journal raises well-being. They recruited 110 adult volunteers and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition wrote down three things they were grateful for every night for a month. Participants in the other condition wrote down three things they had done every night for a month. The researchers then recorded each participant's rating of life satisfaction on a scale from 1 to 10 at the end of the month.

Researchers investigated whether agreeing to a small request makes people more likely to agree to a large one. They recruited 120 homeowners and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Homeowners in one condition were first asked to sign a road-safety petition and two weeks later were asked to put a large sign in their garden. Homeowners in the other condition were only asked to put the large sign in their garden. The researchers then recorded the percentage of homeowners in each group who agreed to display the sign. The results are shown in the table. The difference between the two groups had a p value of 0.41.

rows.group: The group that was first asked to sign the petition
The group that was only asked to display the sign

stimuli.text: Researchers collected data from 450 adults. For each one, they recorded optimism score and the number of days of illness in a year. The correlation between the two measures was r = −0.30.

Researchers investigated whether practice quizzes improve memory more than rereading. They recruited 120 university students and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition read a passage once and then took three practice quizzes on it. Participants in the other condition read the same passage four times. The researchers then recorded the percentage of questions that each participant answered correctly on a test one week later. The results are shown in the table. The difference between the two groups had a p value of 0.01.

columns.label: Mean score on the final test (%)

rows.group: The group that took practice quizzes
The group that reread the passage

stimuli.text: Researchers investigated whether an expected reward reduces children's later interest in drawing. They recruited 60 preschool children who enjoyed drawing and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Children in one condition were promised a certificate for drawing and received it. Children in the other condition drew with no reward mentioned. The researchers then recorded the number of minutes that each child chose to spend drawing during free time one week later.

Researchers collected data from 300 families. For each one, they recorded the warmth of parenting, as rated by observers and the child's self-esteem score. The correlation between the two measures was r = +0.48.

Researchers investigated whether cognitive-behavioral therapy reduces depression. They recruited 90 adults diagnosed with major depressive disorder and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition received twelve weekly sessions of cognitive-behavioral therapy. Participants in the other condition were placed on a waiting list for twelve weeks and were treated afterward. The researchers then recorded each participant's score on a standard depression questionnaire after twelve weeks.

Researchers investigated whether regular aerobic exercise improves memory in older adults. They recruited 100 adults aged 60 to 75 and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition walked briskly for 40 minutes three times a week for six months. Participants in the other condition did gentle stretching for the same amount of time. The researchers then recorded the number of locations that each participant correctly recalled on a spatial memory test.

Read the summary of a hypothetical study, then answer parts A to F.

**Introduction.** Researchers investigated whether keeping a gratitude journal raises well-being. They hypothesized that the type of journal would affect subjective well-being.

**Participants.** The sample was 110 adult volunteers, recruited from one city. All participants gave informed consent, were told they could withdraw at any time, and were debriefed afterward. The plan was approved by an institutional review board.

**Method.** The participants were randomly assigned to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition wrote down three things they were grateful for every night for a month. Participants in the other condition wrote down three things they had done every night for a month. The researchers recorded each participant's rating of life satisfaction on a scale from 1 to 10 at the end of the month.

**Results.** The group that wrote about gratitude: mean life satisfaction (1 to 10) = 7.4. The group that wrote about daily events: mean life satisfaction (1 to 10) = 6.2. The difference was statistically significant (p = 0.01).

Use the three hypothetical sources to answer the question: **Does heavy social media use harm the well-being of teenagers?**

**Source A.** A survey of 1,200 teenagers found a correlation of r = +0.28 between hours of social media use per day and scores on a depression questionnaire. Teenagers who reported feeling lonely tended both to use social media more and to have higher depression scores.

**Source B.** In an experiment, 140 university students were randomly assigned either to limit social media use to 30 minutes a day for three weeks or to continue as usual. At the end, the limited group had a mean loneliness score of 38 and the usual-use group a mean of 45 (p = 0.03).

**Source C.** Researchers interviewed 40 teenagers about their experiences online. Many described feeling worse about themselves after viewing images of peers who seemed more attractive or popular; others described feeling supported by online friends who shared their interests.

questions.stem: A researcher asks whether a shy three-year-old will still be shy at thirty. Which theme of developmental psychology is this?

options.why: A longitudinal study is research that follows the same people and retests them over a long period.
Continuous development is the view that development is a gradual, steady process, like a ramp.
Correct. Stability and change is the developmental question of which traits stay the same through life and which ones alter.
A cross-sectional study is research that compares people of different ages at one point in time.

questions.explanation: Stability and change is the developmental question of which traits stay the same through life and which ones alter.

questions.stem: What does the correlation show?

options.why: A correlation of zero would show no relationship.

options.text: Higher values of the first measure tend to go with lower values of the second
options.why: That would be a negative correlation.

options.text: The first measure causes the second
options.why: A correlation does not show cause and effect.

options.text: Higher values of the first measure tend to go with higher values of the second
options.why: Correct. A positive correlation means the two measures tend to move in the same direction.

questions.explanation: A positive correlation means the two measures tend to move in the same direction.

questions.stem: An eight-month-old learns about a rattle by shaking it, looking at it and putting it in her mouth. Which of Piaget's stages is she in?

options.why: The formal operational stage is Piaget's stage from about age 12 on, in which people can reason about abstract and hypothetical ideas.
The preoperational stage is Piaget's stage from about age 2 to 7, in which children use words and images but cannot yet reason logically.
Correct. The sensorimotor stage is Piaget's stage from birth to about age 2, in which infants know the world through senses and actions.
The concrete operational stage is Piaget's stage from about age 7 to 11, in which children think logically about real objects and events.

questions.explanation: The sensorimotor stage is Piaget's stage from birth to about age 2, in which infants know the world through senses and actions.

questions.stem: Seven students took a memory test. Their scores were 3, 10, 9, 15, 7, 7, 5. What is the range of the scores?

options.why: That is the median.
That is the mean.
Correct. Subtract the lowest score from the highest.
That is the highest score.

questions.explanation: In order, the scores are 3, 5, 7, 7, 9, 10, 15. Subtract the lowest score from the highest. The one very high score pulls the mean (8) above the median (7), so the distribution is positively skewed.

questions.stem: After a stroke, Mrs. Cho speaks fluently, but her sentences make no sense and she cannot understand others. Which area was most likely damaged?

options.why: Hemispheric specialization is the tendency for each side of the brain to handle certain functions, such as language in the left hemisphere.
Contralateral control is the arrangement in which each hemisphere controls the opposite side of the body.
Broca's area is the area in the left frontal lobe that controls speech production.
Correct. Wernicke's area is the area in the left temporal lobe that controls language comprehension.

questions.explanation: Wernicke's area is the area in the left temporal lobe that controls language comprehension.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes an optimistic explanatory style?

options.text: The feeling of being worse off than the people one compares oneself with
options.why: That describes relative deprivation.

options.text: The habit of explaining bad events as lasting, affecting everything and caused by oneself
options.why: That describes a pessimistic explanatory style.

options.text: The habit of explaining bad events as temporary, specific and caused by outside factors
options.why: Correct. This is what an optimistic explanatory style means.

options.text: The tendency to explain our own behavior by the situation but other people's behavior by their traits
options.why: That describes the actor-observer bias.

questions.explanation: An optimistic explanatory style is the habit of explaining bad events as temporary, specific and caused by outside factors.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the influence of a researcher's expectations on the results of a study?

options.why: Self-report bias is the inaccuracy that arises when people describe their own behavior or feelings.
Overconfidence is the tendency to be more certain than correct about one's own judgments.
Social desirability bias is the tendency of participants to answer in a way that makes them look good.
Correct. Experimenter bias is the influence of a researcher's expectations on the results of a study.

questions.explanation: Experimenter bias is the influence of a researcher's expectations on the results of a study.

questions.stem: Severe stress early in life switches off a gene in a rat pup, even though the pup's DNA sequence is unchanged. Which field studies this kind of effect?

options.why: Eugenics is the discredited movement that misused ideas about heredity to argue for selective breeding of humans.
An adoption study is research that compares adopted children with their biological and adoptive relatives.
Correct. Epigenetics is the study of how the environment changes whether genes are expressed without changing the DNA itself.
A twin study is research that compares identical and fraternal twins to estimate the influence of heredity.

questions.explanation: Epigenetics is the study of how the environment changes whether genes are expressed without changing the DNA itself.

questions.stem: Can the researchers conclude that conscientiousness score on a personality inventory causes a change in grade point average?

options.text: Yes, because the correlation is not zero
options.why: Any nonzero correlation still leaves the cause unknown.

options.text: Yes, because the sample was large
options.why: A large sample does not turn a correlation into evidence of causation.

options.text: No, because correlations can only be calculated in experiments
options.why: Correlations are calculated in non-experimental studies.

options.text: No, because a correlation does not show cause and effect
options.why: Correct. Without manipulating a variable and assigning subjects at random, other explanations cannot be ruled out.

questions.explanation: Without manipulating a variable and assigning subjects at random, other explanations cannot be ruled out.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the comparing of oneself with people who are doing worse?

options.why: Correct. Downward social comparison is the comparing of oneself with people who are doing worse.
A dispositional attribution is an explanation of behavior that points to the person's own traits or character.
A situational attribution is an explanation of behavior that points to outside circumstances.
A self-fulfilling prophecy is an expectation that leads a person to act in ways that make the expectation come true.

questions.explanation: Downward social comparison is the comparing of oneself with people who are doing worse.

questions.stem: In myasthenia gravis, receptors for one neurotransmitter are blocked, which causes muscle weakness. Which neurotransmitter is affected?

options.why: Dopamine is the neurotransmitter that influences movement, attention, and feelings of reward.
Serotonin is the neurotransmitter that affects mood, hunger and sleep.
Correct. Acetylcholine is the neurotransmitter that enables muscle movement, learning and memory.
Endorphins is the neurotransmitters that reduce pain and increase pleasure.

questions.explanation: Acetylcholine is the neurotransmitter that enables muscle movement, learning and memory.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes effect size?

options.text: The group in an experiment that does not receive the treatment and is used for comparison
options.why: That describes the control group.

options.text: A procedure in which neither the participants nor the researchers who deal with them know who is in which condition
options.why: That describes a double-blind procedure.

options.text: A factor other than the independent variable that differs between groups and could explain the results
options.why: That describes a confounding variable.

options.text: The measure of how large the difference or relationship found in a study is
options.why: Correct. This is what effect size means.

questions.explanation: Effect size is the measure of how large the difference or relationship found in a study is.

questions.stem: In which structure of the inner ear do hair cells convert sound vibrations into neural signals?

options.why: Correct. The cochlea is the coiled, fluid-filled tube in the inner ear where sound waves become neural impulses.
Amplitude is the height of a sound wave, which determines loudness.
Frequency is the number of sound waves per second, which determines pitch.
Wavelength is the distance from one wave peak to the next, which determines the hue of light.

questions.explanation: The cochlea is the coiled, fluid-filled tube in the inner ear where sound waves become neural impulses.

questions.stem: People who move next to a railway are woken by trains at first but soon sleep through the noise. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: Biological preparedness is the inborn readiness to learn some associations, such as taste and nausea, more easily than others.
A taste aversion is a learned dislike of a food that was followed by illness.
Counterconditioning is the replacing of an unwanted response to a stimulus with a new response, by pairing the stimulus with something pleasant.
Correct. Habituation is the decrease in response to a stimulus that is presented over and over.

questions.explanation: Habituation is the decrease in response to a stimulus that is presented over and over.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the hormone released by fat cells that signals fullness and reduces hunger?

options.why: Correct. Leptin is the hormone released by fat cells that signals fullness and reduces hunger.
Ghrelin is the hormone released by an empty stomach that increases hunger.
Adrenaline is the hormone released by the adrenal glands that raises heart rate and energy during stress.
Melatonin is the hormone released by the pineal gland that makes a person sleepy.

questions.explanation: Leptin is the hormone released by fat cells that signals fullness and reduces hunger.

questions.stem: After being shouted at by her boss, Gia goes home and shouts at her younger brother. Which defense mechanism is this?

options.why: Correct. Displacement is the defense mechanism of shifting an impulse from its real target to a safer one.
Rationalization is the defense mechanism of giving a comfortable excuse in place of the real reason for a behavior.
Denial is the defense mechanism of refusing to accept a painful reality.
Projection is the defense mechanism of seeing one's own unacceptable impulses in other people.

questions.explanation: Displacement is the defense mechanism of shifting an impulse from its real target to a safer one.

questions.stem: Although he is not hungry, Karl buys a cake because it looks and smells delicious. Which theory of motivation best explains this?

options.why: Correct. Incentive theory is the theory that behavior is pulled by rewards from outside the person.
Instinct theory is the theory that behavior is driven by fixed, inborn patterns that are not learned.
Self-determination theory is the theory that people are motivated by needs for competence, autonomy and relatedness, either from within or from outside.
The Yerkes-Dodson law is the principle that performance is best at a moderate level of arousal.

questions.explanation: Incentive theory is the theory that behavior is pulled by rewards from outside the person.

questions.stem: A mother's employer changes her to night shifts, so she sees her son less. In ecological systems theory, her workplace is part of which system?

options.why: The macrosystem is in ecological systems theory, the cultural values, laws and customs that surround a child.
The chronosystem is in ecological systems theory, the life stage and historical events that affect a child.
The microsystem is in ecological systems theory, the groups that have direct contact with the child, such as family and school.
Correct. The exosystem is in ecological systems theory, the settings that affect a child indirectly, such as a parent's workplace.

questions.explanation: The exosystem is in ecological systems theory, the settings that affect a child indirectly, such as a parent's workplace.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the discomfort a person feels when their actions and attitudes conflict, which motivates a change in one of them?

options.why: Out-group homogeneity bias is the tendency to see the members of other groups as all alike.
Belief perseverance is the tendency to hold on to a belief even after the evidence for it has been discredited.
Confirmation bias is the tendency to search for and favor information that supports what one already believes.
Correct. Cognitive dissonance is the discomfort a person feels when their actions and attitudes conflict, which motivates a change in one of them.

questions.explanation: Cognitive dissonance is the discomfort a person feels when their actions and attitudes conflict, which motivates a change in one of them.

questions.stem: Over ten trials in which a light is followed by a puff of air, a rabbit begins to blink at the light. This learning stage is called which of the following?

options.why: Spontaneous recovery is the reappearance of a weakened conditioned response after a rest period.
Stimulus generalization is the tendency to respond to stimuli that are similar to the conditioned stimulus.
Correct. Acquisition is in classical conditioning, the first stage, in which the neutral stimulus is paired with the unconditioned stimulus and the response is learned.
Extinction is the weakening of a conditioned response when the conditioned stimulus is repeatedly presented alone.

questions.explanation: Acquisition is in classical conditioning, the first stage, in which the neutral stimulus is paired with the unconditioned stimulus and the response is learned.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the part of working memory that directs attention and coordinates the other parts?

options.why: Long-term potentiation is the strengthening of the connections between neurons after repeated activation, which is the biological basis of memory.
Correct. The central executive is the part of working memory that directs attention and coordinates the other parts.
The phonological loop is the part of working memory that briefly holds spoken and written words.
The visuospatial sketchpad is the part of working memory that briefly holds images and spatial information.

questions.explanation: The central executive is the part of working memory that directs attention and coordinates the other parts.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes the amygdala?

options.text: The wrinkled outer layer of the brain, which handles thinking, perception and voluntary movement
options.why: That describes the cerebral cortex.

options.text: The band of fibers that connects the two hemispheres of the brain
options.why: That describes the corpus callosum.

options.text: The structure that processes fear and aggression
options.why: Correct. This is what the amygdala means.

options.text: The structure that regulates hunger, thirst, body temperature and sexual behavior and controls the pituitary gland
options.why: That describes the hypothalamus.

questions.explanation: The amygdala is the structure that processes fear and aggression.

questions.stem: Which stage of sleep is called paradoxical sleep because the brain is active while the body is nearly paralyzed?

options.why: Correct. REM sleep is the sleep stage with rapid eye movements, vivid dreams, an active brain and relaxed muscles.
NREM stage 1 is the brief, light first stage of sleep, in which a person may have hypnagogic sensations such as falling.
The circadian rhythm is the body's roughly 24-hour cycle of wakefulness and sleep.
REM rebound is the tendency to have more REM sleep after being deprived of it.

questions.explanation: REM sleep is the sleep stage with rapid eye movements, vivid dreams, an active brain and relaxed muscles.

questions.stem: Which of the following would be a confounding variable in this study?

options.text: Each one was assigned to a condition at random
options.why: Random assignment reduces confounding; it is not a confound.

options.text: The rooms used for the groups of five were much noisier
options.why: Correct. It differs between the groups along with the independent variable, so it could explain the results instead.

options.text: The two groups differed in the reporting of an emergency at the end of the study
options.why: That is the dependent variable, the result being measured.

options.text: One group differed from the other in the number of other people present
options.why: That is the independent variable itself.

questions.explanation: It differs between the groups along with the independent variable, so it could explain the results instead.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the Gestalt principle that we fill in gaps to see a complete, whole object?

options.why: Similarity is the Gestalt principle that we group together objects that look alike.
Proximity is the Gestalt principle that we group together objects that are near each other.
Correct. Closure is the Gestalt principle that we fill in gaps to see a complete, whole object.
Figure and ground is the Gestalt principle that we organize a scene into an object that stands out and its background.

questions.explanation: Closure is the Gestalt principle that we fill in gaps to see a complete, whole object.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes identity diffusion?

options.text: The identity status of a person who has neither explored options nor made a commitment
options.why: Correct. This is what identity diffusion means.

options.text: The identity status of a person who is actively exploring options but has not yet made a commitment
options.why: That describes identity moratorium.

options.text: The identity status of a person who has made a commitment without exploring options
options.why: That describes identity foreclosure.

options.text: The identity status of a person who has explored options and made a commitment
options.why: That describes identity achievement.

questions.explanation: Identity diffusion is the identity status of a person who has neither explored options nor made a commitment.

questions.stem: A day after meeting twelve new people, Joy remembers only the names of the first two she met. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: Correct. The primacy effect is the tendency to remember the first items in a list well.
The serial position effect is the tendency to remember the first and last items in a list better than the middle ones.
The recency effect is the tendency to remember the last items in a list well.
The spacing effect is the finding that study spread over time produces better long-term memory than study crammed together.

questions.explanation: The primacy effect is the tendency to remember the first items in a list well.

questions.stem: A tumor just above the ear disrupts a patient's ability to process sounds. Which lobes are affected?

options.why: The frontal lobes is the lobes behind the forehead, which handle planning, judgment and voluntary movement.
Correct. The temporal lobes is the lobes above the ears, which process sound and help recognize language.
The occipital lobes is the lobes at the back of the head, which process visual information.
The motor cortex is the strip at the rear of the frontal lobes that controls voluntary movements.

questions.explanation: The temporal lobes is the lobes above the ears, which process sound and help recognize language.

questions.stem: After witnessing a violent event, a man with no head injury cannot remember his name or anything about his past. Which disorder does this suggest?

options.why: Correct. Dissociative amnesia is the disorder in which a person cannot remember important personal information, usually after trauma and with no physical cause, sometimes with travel away from home (fugue).
Hoarding disorder is the disorder in which a person cannot throw away possessions, so that living spaces become cluttered.
Posttraumatic stress disorder is the disorder in which a person has flashbacks, nightmares, watchfulness and avoidance for more than a month after a terrifying event.
Obsessive-compulsive disorder is the disorder in which a person has unwanted repeated thoughts and feels driven to perform repeated actions.

questions.explanation: Dissociative amnesia is the disorder in which a person cannot remember important personal information, usually after trauma and with no physical cause, sometimes with travel away from home (fugue).

questions.stem: A fifty-year-old mentors younger colleagues and volunteers as a youth coach, wanting to give something to the next generation. Which of Erikson's stages is this?

options.why: Intimacy versus isolation is Erikson's stage in young adulthood, in which people seek close, lasting relationships.
Identity versus role confusion is Erikson's stage in adolescence, in which teenagers work out who they are.
Correct. Generativity versus stagnation is Erikson's stage in middle adulthood, in which people seek to contribute to the world through family and work.
Integrity versus despair is Erikson's stage in late adulthood, in which people look back on life with satisfaction or regret.

questions.explanation: Generativity versus stagnation is Erikson's stage in middle adulthood, in which people seek to contribute to the world through family and work.

questions.stem: To remember the term 'hippocampus', Sol links it to a hippo on a campus who never forgets his classes. Which technique is he using?

options.why: Maintenance rehearsal is the repeating of information over and over to keep it in short-term memory.
Highly superior autobiographical memory is the rare ability to recall almost every day of one's life in detail.
Autobiographical memory is the memory of the events of one's own life.
Correct. Elaborative rehearsal is the linking of new information to existing knowledge and meaning to store it in long-term memory.

questions.explanation: Elaborative rehearsal is the linking of new information to existing knowledge and meaning to store it in long-term memory.

questions.stem: Neither the participants nor the assistants who recorded the results knew which condition each participant was in. What is this procedure called?

options.why: In a single-blind procedure only the participants are unaware.
Random sampling is how participants are chosen from a population.
That is a therapy technique, not a research control.
Correct. Keeping both participants and researchers unaware of the conditions reduces bias from expectations.

questions.explanation: Keeping both participants and researchers unaware of the conditions reduces bias from expectations.

questions.stem: In Pavlov's experiments, dogs salivated to food, and later to a tone that had been paired with food. Salivating to the tone alone was which of the following?

options.why: The unconditioned response is in classical conditioning, the natural, unlearned response to a stimulus.
The unconditioned stimulus is in classical conditioning, the stimulus that triggers a response naturally, without learning.
The conditioned stimulus is in classical conditioning, the originally neutral stimulus that triggers a response after being paired with another stimulus.
Correct. The conditioned response is in classical conditioning, the learned response to a previously neutral stimulus.

questions.explanation: The conditioned response is in classical conditioning, the learned response to a previously neutral stimulus.

questions.stem: Why is this study not an experiment?

options.text: The researchers did not manipulate a variable or randomly assign anyone to conditions
options.why: Correct. An experiment requires a manipulated independent variable and random assignment.
Experiments also use numerical data.
Sample size does not determine the research method.
Experiments also test hypotheses.

questions.explanation: An experiment requires a manipulated independent variable and random assignment.

questions.stem: Which structure at the back of the eye contains the rods and cones?

options.why: Correct. The retina is the light-sensitive inner surface at the back of the eye that contains the receptor cells.
Rods is the receptor cells that detect black, white and gray and work in dim light and peripheral vision.
The fovea is the central point of the retina, where cones are packed most densely and vision is sharpest.
Cones is the receptor cells that detect color and fine detail and work in bright light.

questions.explanation: The retina is the light-sensitive inner surface at the back of the eye that contains the receptor cells.

questions.stem: Eight-year-old Max cannot stay seated, blurts out answers and loses focus within minutes, far more than other children his age. Which disorder does this suggest?

options.why: Bulimia nervosa is the eating disorder in which a person binges on food and then makes up for it by vomiting, fasting or excessive exercise.
Anorexia nervosa is the eating disorder in which a person restricts food to the point of being dangerously underweight, with an intense fear of gaining weight.
A specific learning disorder is the neurodevelopmental disorder marked by persistent difficulty in reading, writing or math despite normal intelligence.
Correct. Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder is the neurodevelopmental disorder marked by inattention, hyperactivity and impulsiveness.

questions.explanation: Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder is the neurodevelopmental disorder marked by inattention, hyperactivity and impulsiveness.

questions.stem: An advertisement for a car shows a famous athlete smiling beside it and gives no facts. Which route to persuasion is it using?

options.why: Normative social influence is the influence that comes from a person's desire to gain approval or avoid rejection.
Correct. The peripheral route to persuasion is persuasion that works through surface cues, such as an attractive or famous speaker.
The door-in-the-face technique is the strategy of making a large request that will be refused so that a smaller request is more likely to be accepted.
The halo effect is the tendency for one good quality of a person to make us assume they have other good qualities.

questions.explanation: The peripheral route to persuasion is persuasion that works through surface cues, such as an attractive or famous speaker.

questions.stem: Before the study could begin, a committee at the university reviewed the plan to make sure the children would be protected from harm. What is this committee called?

options.why: That is a comparison condition.
A confederate is someone who secretly works for the researcher.
That is a discussion group used to collect opinions.
Correct. An institutional review board must approve research with human participants.

questions.explanation: An institutional review board must approve research with human participants.

questions.stem: What is the independent variable in this study?

options.why: This is a procedure for forming the groups, not a variable.
Correct. The independent variable is the factor the researchers changed between the two conditions.

options.text: The number of participants in the study
options.why: This is the sample size, not a variable the researchers changed.
This was measured, not manipulated: it is the dependent variable.

questions.explanation: The independent variable is the factor the researchers changed between the two conditions.

questions.stem: Each night, Noor writes down three things she is thankful for, and over time she feels happier. Which practice is this?

options.why: Subjective well-being is a person's own evaluation of how happy and satisfied they are with life.
Posttraumatic growth is the positive psychological change that some people experience after struggling with a very difficult event.
Correct. Gratitude is the appreciation of the good things in one's life, the practice of which raises well-being.
Signature strengths is the positive character traits, such as kindness or curiosity, that are most central to a particular person.

questions.explanation: Gratitude is the appreciation of the good things in one's life, the practice of which raises well-being.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes prosopagnosia?

options.text: A rare form of color blindness in which a person sees only shades of gray
options.why: That describes monochromatism.

options.text: A form of color vision deficiency in which one of the three types of cones does not work
options.why: That describes dichromatism.

options.text: The theory that the retina has three types of color receptors, sensitive to red, green and blue
options.why: That describes the trichromatic theory.

options.text: The inability to recognize faces, even familiar ones, after brain damage
options.why: Correct. This is what prosopagnosia means.

questions.explanation: Prosopagnosia is the inability to recognize faces, even familiar ones, after brain damage.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes a survey?

options.text: The repeating of a study with different participants to see whether the finding holds
options.why: That describes replication.

options.text: The research method of collecting self-reported attitudes or behaviors from a sample by asking questions
options.why: Correct. This is what a survey means.

options.text: A testable prediction about the relationship between variables
options.why: That describes a hypothesis.

options.text: The quality of a claim that it could be shown to be wrong by evidence
options.why: That describes falsifiability.

questions.explanation: A survey is the research method of collecting self-reported attitudes or behaviors from a sample by asking questions.

questions.stem: Which statement about the results is best supported?

options.text: The study shows that the two conditions always give identical results
options.why: A non-significant result does not show that there is no effect at all.

options.text: The difference between the groups is not statistically significant, so it could easily be due to chance
options.why: Correct. A p value above 0.05 means a difference this size would often occur by chance alone.

options.text: The independent variable had a large effect
options.why: The averages are close and the difference is not significant.

options.text: The difference between the groups is statistically significant
options.why: A p value of 0.41 is far above 0.05.

questions.explanation: A p value above 0.05 means a difference this size would often occur by chance alone.

questions.stem: A second study of a different pair of measures finds r = +0.50. Which relationship is stronger?

options.text: The relationship in the first study, because its coefficient is closer to zero
options.why: A coefficient closer to zero shows a weaker relationship.

options.text: The relationship in the second study, because its coefficient is farther from zero
options.why: Correct. The strength of a correlation is its distance from zero, whatever the sign.

options.text: The relationship with the negative sign, whatever its size
options.why: The sign shows direction, not strength.

options.text: Neither, because relationships with different signs cannot be compared
options.why: Strength can be compared by distance from zero.

questions.explanation: The strength of a correlation is its distance from zero, whatever the sign.

questions.stem: Ines cannot stand doing the same task twice and becomes restless whenever life is predictable. Which form of sensation seeking is this?

options.why: Experience seeking is the form of sensation seeking that involves a desire for new experiences through travel, art and unusual lifestyles.
Thrill and adventure seeking is the form of sensation seeking that involves a desire for risky physical activities.
Disinhibition is the form of sensation seeking that involves a loss of self-restraint, as at wild parties.
Correct. Boredom susceptibility is the form of sensation seeking that involves a strong dislike of repetition and routine.

questions.explanation: Boredom susceptibility is the form of sensation seeking that involves a strong dislike of repetition and routine.

questions.stem: A toddler who knows the word 'dog' sees a cow for the first time and calls it a dog. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: A schema is a mental framework that organizes and interprets information.
Accommodation is the changing of an existing schema to fit new information.
Correct. Assimilation is the interpretation of a new experience in terms of an existing schema.
A concept is a mental grouping of similar objects, events, ideas or people.

questions.explanation: Assimilation is the interpretation of a new experience in terms of an existing schema.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes infantile amnesia?

options.text: A progressive brain disease that destroys memory and then other mental abilities
options.why: That describes Alzheimer's disease.

options.text: The inability of adults to remember events from the first few years of life
options.why: Correct. This is what infantile amnesia means.

options.text: The inability to form new memories after an injury or illness
options.why: That describes anterograde amnesia.

options.text: The loss of memories from before an injury or illness
options.why: That describes retrograde amnesia.

questions.explanation: Infantile amnesia is the inability of adults to remember events from the first few years of life.

questions.stem: Which statement about the results is best supported?

options.text: The difference between the groups is statistically significant, so it is unlikely to be due to chance
options.why: Correct. A p value below 0.05 means a difference this large would rarely occur by chance alone.

options.text: The results prove that every individual in the first group differed from every individual in the second
options.why: The table reports group averages, not individual scores.

options.text: The difference between the groups is probably due to chance
options.why: A p value of 0.01 is below 0.05, so chance is an unlikely explanation.

options.text: The two groups had the same average result
options.why: The table shows different averages.

questions.explanation: A p value below 0.05 means a difference this large would rarely occur by chance alone.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as a simple thinking shortcut that is fast but can lead to errors?

options.why: Executive functions is the mental processes used to plan, organize and carry out goal-directed behavior.
An algorithm is a step-by-step procedure that guarantees a solution.
Correct. A heuristic is a simple thinking shortcut that is fast but can lead to errors.
Divergent thinking is thinking that produces many possible answers to a problem.

questions.explanation: A heuristic is a simple thinking shortcut that is fast but can lead to errors.

questions.stem: A client with borderline personality disorder learns mindfulness, ways of tolerating distress and ways of regulating emotions. Which therapy is this?

options.why: Correct. Dialectical behavior therapy is the therapy that teaches skills for tolerating distress and controlling emotions, often used for borderline personality disorder.
The cognitive triad is the pattern of negative thoughts about oneself, the world and the future that is found in depression.
Rational emotive behavior therapy is the confrontational cognitive therapy, developed by Ellis, that actively challenges a client's irrational beliefs.
Cognitive-behavioral therapy is the therapy that combines changing self-defeating thoughts with changing behavior.

questions.explanation: Dialectical behavior therapy is the therapy that teaches skills for tolerating distress and controlling emotions, often used for borderline personality disorder.

questions.stem: Leah paints every evening simply because she loves doing it. Which kind of motivation is this?

options.why: An approach-approach conflict is a conflict in which a person must choose between two attractive options.
An approach-avoidance conflict is a conflict in which one option has both attractive and unattractive features.
An avoidance-avoidance conflict is a conflict in which a person must choose between two unattractive options.
Correct. Intrinsic motivation is the desire to do something for its own sake, because it is enjoyable or satisfying.

questions.explanation: Intrinsic motivation is the desire to do something for its own sake, because it is enjoyable or satisfying.

questions.stem: Before the study could begin, a committee at the university reviewed the plan to make sure the children would be protected from harm. What is this committee called?

options.why: That is a comparison condition.
That is a discussion group used to collect opinions.
A confederate is someone who secretly works for the researcher.
Correct. An institutional review board must approve research with human participants.

questions.explanation: An institutional review board must approve research with human participants.

questions.stem: To choose 500 students for a survey, a researcher uses a computer to pick names from the list of all students in the country. Which procedure is this?

options.why: Sampling bias is a flaw in selecting participants that makes the sample unlike the population.
A convenience sample is a sample made up of whoever is easiest for the researcher to reach.
Correct. Random sampling is the selecting of participants so that every member of the population has an equal chance of being chosen.
A representative sample is a sample whose characteristics match those of the population it is drawn from.

questions.explanation: Random sampling is the selecting of participants so that every member of the population has an equal chance of being chosen.

questions.stem: What does the correlation show?

options.text: Higher values of the first measure tend to go with higher values of the second
options.why: Correct. A positive correlation means the two measures tend to move in the same direction.

options.text: Higher values of the first measure tend to go with lower values of the second
options.why: That would be a negative correlation.

options.text: The first measure causes the second
options.why: A correlation does not show cause and effect.
A correlation of zero would show no relationship.

questions.explanation: A positive correlation means the two measures tend to move in the same direction.

questions.stem: In the 1940s, surgeons cut the connections to patients' frontal lobes to calm them, often leaving them permanently listless. Which procedure was this?

options.why: Psychotropic medication is any drug that acts on the brain to treat the symptoms of a psychological disorder.
Correct. A lobotomy is the now-abandoned form of psychosurgery that cut the nerves connecting the frontal lobes to the rest of the brain.
Electroconvulsive therapy is the treatment for severe depression in which a brief electric current is passed through the brain of an anesthetized patient.
Transcranial magnetic stimulation is the treatment in which repeated magnetic pulses are applied to the surface of the brain to treat depression.

questions.explanation: A lobotomy is the now-abandoned form of psychosurgery that cut the nerves connecting the frontal lobes to the rest of the brain.

questions.stem: A therapist and client rank situations from 'looking at a picture of a spider' to 'holding a spider.' What is this ranked list called?

options.why: Correct. A fear hierarchy is a list of feared situations arranged from the least to the most frightening.
A token economy is the behavioral system in which people earn tokens for desired behavior and exchange them for rewards.
Aversion therapy is the behavioral treatment that pairs an unwanted behavior with an unpleasant stimulus.
Systematic desensitization is the exposure therapy that pairs relaxation with a graded series of anxiety-arousing stimuli.

questions.explanation: A fear hierarchy is a list of feared situations arranged from the least to the most frightening.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes the resistance phase?

options.text: The second phase of the general adaptation syndrome, in which the body stays highly aroused to cope with a continuing stressor
options.why: Correct. This is what the resistance phase means.

options.text: Selye's three-phase description of the body's response to long-term stress: alarm, resistance and exhaustion
options.why: That describes the general adaptation syndrome.

options.text: The first phase of the general adaptation syndrome, in which the sympathetic nervous system is suddenly activated
options.why: That describes the alarm reaction.

options.text: The third phase of the general adaptation syndrome, in which the body's resources run out and illness becomes more likely
options.why: That describes the exhaustion phase.

questions.explanation: The resistance phase is the second phase of the general adaptation syndrome, in which the body stays highly aroused to cope with a continuing stressor.

questions.stem: Ice cream sales and drownings rise together, but both are caused by hot weather. Which problem does this illustrate?

options.why: Correct. The third variable problem is the possibility that an unmeasured factor causes the relationship between two correlated variables.
The directionality problem is the difficulty in a correlational study of knowing which variable influences the other.
A negative correlation is a relationship in which one variable rises as the other falls.
The correlation coefficient is the number from −1.00 to +1.00 that shows the direction and strength of a relationship.

questions.explanation: The third variable problem is the possibility that an unmeasured factor causes the relationship between two correlated variables.

questions.stem: Flat affect, loss of motivation and social withdrawal involve the absence of normal behaviors. Which kind of symptom are they?

options.why: The dopamine hypothesis is the idea that schizophrenia involves excessive activity of the neurotransmitter dopamine.
Correct. A negative symptom is a symptom of schizophrenia that takes away a normal behavior, such as emotional expression or motivation.
An acute onset is the sudden appearance of schizophrenia, often after stress, from which recovery is more likely.
A chronic course is the slow, gradual development of schizophrenia, from which recovery is less likely.

questions.explanation: A negative symptom is a symptom of schizophrenia that takes away a normal behavior, such as emotional expression or motivation.

questions.stem: Two two-year-olds sit next to each other, each building with their own blocks and not speaking. Which kind of play is this?

options.why: The imaginary audience is the belief of adolescents that everyone is watching and judging them.
Pretend play is the play in which children act out imaginary roles and situations.
Correct. Parallel play is the play of young children who play side by side without interacting.
The social clock is a culture's preferred timing for life events such as marriage, parenthood and retirement.

questions.explanation: Parallel play is the play of young children who play side by side without interacting.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes fine motor skills?

options.text: A newborn's automatic turning of the head toward a touch on the cheek, to find food
options.why: That describes the rooting reflex.

options.text: The movements that use large muscles, such as crawling, walking and jumping
options.why: That describes gross motor skills.

options.text: A harmful agent, such as alcohol or a virus, that can damage an embryo or fetus
options.why: That describes a teratogen.

options.text: The movements that use small muscles, such as grasping a crayon or buttoning a shirt
options.why: Correct. This is what fine motor skills means.

questions.explanation: Fine motor skills is the movements that use small muscles, such as grasping a crayon or buttoning a shirt.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes transcendence?

options.text: The category of character strengths that includes love, kindness and social intelligence
options.why: That describes humanity.

options.text: The category of character strengths that includes teamwork, fairness and leadership
options.why: That describes justice.

options.text: The category of character strengths that includes gratitude, hope, humor and appreciation of beauty
options.why: Correct. This is what transcendence means.

options.text: The category of character strengths that includes forgiveness, humility and self-control
options.why: That describes temperance.

questions.explanation: Transcendence is the category of character strengths that includes gratitude, hope, humor and appreciation of beauty.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the therapy in which several clients meet together with a therapist and benefit from each other's support?

options.why: Active listening is the technique of echoing, restating and seeking clarification of what the client says.
Correct. Group therapy is the therapy in which several clients meet together with a therapist and benefit from each other's support.
Hypnosis is a state of heightened suggestibility that can help reduce pain and anxiety but does not reliably recover memories.
Person-centered therapy is the humanistic therapy in which the therapist provides acceptance and empathy so that the client can grow.

questions.explanation: Group therapy is the therapy in which several clients meet together with a therapist and benefit from each other's support.

questions.stem: Which group served as the control group?

options.text: The group on the waiting list
options.why: Correct. The control group is the comparison group that does not receive the treatment being tested.
Only the comparison group is the control group.

options.text: Neither group, because the study had no comparison condition
options.why: The second condition is the comparison.
This group received the treatment being tested: it is the experimental group.

questions.explanation: The control group is the comparison group that does not receive the treatment being tested.

questions.stem: Neither the participants nor the assistants who recorded the results knew which condition each participant was in. What is this procedure called?

options.why: In a single-blind procedure only the participants are unaware.
That is a therapy technique, not a research control.
Random sampling is how participants are chosen from a population.
Correct. Keeping both participants and researchers unaware of the conditions reduces bias from expectations.

questions.explanation: Keeping both participants and researchers unaware of the conditions reduces bias from expectations.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes the thalamus?

options.text: The network of neurons in the brainstem that controls arousal and alertness
options.why: That describes the reticular activating system.

options.text: The brain's sensory relay station, which directs incoming signals to the cortex
options.why: Correct. This is what the thalamus means.

options.text: The base of the brainstem, which controls heartbeat and breathing
options.why: That describes the medulla.

options.text: The master gland of the endocrine system, which is controlled by the hypothalamus
options.why: That describes the pituitary gland.

questions.explanation: The thalamus is the brain's sensory relay station, which directs incoming signals to the cortex.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the process in which the sending neuron reabsorbs leftover neurotransmitters from the synapse?

options.why: The refractory period is the brief pause after a neuron fires during which it cannot fire again.
Correct. Reuptake is the process in which the sending neuron reabsorbs leftover neurotransmitters from the synapse.
The action potential is the brief electrical charge that travels down the axon when a neuron fires.
The resting potential is the stable negative charge inside a neuron when it is not firing.

questions.explanation: Reuptake is the process in which the sending neuron reabsorbs leftover neurotransmitters from the synapse.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes test-retest reliability?

options.text: The consistency of scores between two halves of the same test
options.why: That describes split-half reliability.

options.text: The extent to which test scores forecast the future performance they are meant to predict
options.why: That describes predictive validity.

options.text: The consistency of scores when the same people take the same test twice
options.why: Correct. This is what test-retest reliability means.

options.text: The extent to which a test measures the concept it claims to measure
options.why: That describes construct validity.

questions.explanation: Test-retest reliability is the consistency of scores when the same people take the same test twice.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the nonreproductive traits of sexual maturity, such as body hair and a deeper voice?

options.why: Menarche is a girl's first menstrual period.
Menopause is the natural end of menstruation and of the ability to reproduce, usually around age 50.
Correct. Secondary sex characteristics is the nonreproductive traits of sexual maturity, such as body hair and a deeper voice.
Primary sex characteristics is the body structures, such as ovaries and testes, that make reproduction possible.

questions.explanation: Secondary sex characteristics is the nonreproductive traits of sexual maturity, such as body hair and a deeper voice.

questions.stem: A therapist selects a treatment because controlled studies show it works for the client's disorder and it fits the client's preferences. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: Correct. Evidence-based practice is the choosing of treatments on the basis of research, clinical skill and the client's own values.
Deinstitutionalization is the movement, begun in the 1950s, of patients out of psychiatric hospitals and into community care.
The therapeutic alliance is the bond of trust and cooperation between therapist and client.
Cultural humility is a therapist's openness to learning about a client's culture and awareness of the limits of their own view.

questions.explanation: Evidence-based practice is the choosing of treatments on the basis of research, clinical skill and the client's own values.

questions.stem: Kim knows that Paris is the capital of France, although she cannot remember when she learned it. Which kind of memory is this?

options.why: Episodic memory is the explicit memory of personally experienced events.
Prospective memory is the memory to carry out a planned action in the future.
Correct. Semantic memory is the explicit memory of facts and general knowledge.
Procedural memory is the implicit memory of how to perform skills and actions.

questions.explanation: Semantic memory is the explicit memory of facts and general knowledge.

questions.stem: Each of twenty witnesses to an accident assumes that someone else has already called for help, so nobody calls. Which concept explains their thinking?

options.why: Correct. Diffusion of responsibility is the reduced sense of personal duty to act when other people are present.
Group polarization is the strengthening of a group's existing opinions after the members discuss them.
Deindividuation is the loss of self-awareness and self-restraint in group situations that provide arousal and anonymity.
Groupthink is the kind of thinking in which the desire for agreement in a group overrides a realistic evaluation of alternatives.

questions.explanation: Diffusion of responsibility is the reduced sense of personal duty to act when other people are present.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes long-term memory?

options.text: The relatively permanent and limitless store of knowledge, skills and experiences
options.why: Correct. This is what long-term memory means.

options.text: The memory store that briefly holds a few items, about seven, before they are stored or forgotten
options.why: That describes short-term memory.

options.text: The sensory memory of a sound, which lasts three or four seconds
options.why: That describes echoic memory.

options.text: The brief sensory memory of a visual image, which lasts a few tenths of a second
options.why: That describes iconic memory.

questions.explanation: Long-term memory is the relatively permanent and limitless store of knowledge, skills and experiences.

questions.stem: In a town where most people earn modest incomes and a few earn millions, the mean income is far above the median. Which shape does the distribution have?

options.why: The mode is the score that occurs most often.
The mean is the arithmetic average of a set of scores.
The range is the difference between the highest and lowest scores.
Correct. A positive skew is a distribution with a few extremely high scores, which pull the mean above the median.

questions.explanation: A positive skew is a distribution with a few extremely high scores, which pull the mean above the median.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the field that studies how behavior, thoughts and emotions affect physical health and illness?

options.why: The tend-and-befriend response is the response to stress of caring for others and seeking social support.
Distress is the negative stress that harms well-being and performance.
A stressor is an event or situation that a person sees as threatening or challenging.
Correct. Health psychology is the field that studies how behavior, thoughts and emotions affect physical health and illness.

questions.explanation: Health psychology is the field that studies how behavior, thoughts and emotions affect physical health and illness.

questions.title: Article analysis: a study of subjective well-being

parts.prompt: Identify the research method used in the study.

rubric.criterion: Identifies the method as an experiment.
rubric.example: The study is an experiment: the researchers manipulated a variable and randomly assigned the subjects to conditions.

parts.prompt: State the operational definition of subjective well-being.

rubric.criterion: States how the variable was measured in this study.
rubric.example: Subjective well-being was defined as each participant's rating of life satisfaction on a scale from 1 to 10 at the end of the month.

parts.prompt: Describe the meaning of the difference between the two group averages.

rubric.criterion: Accurately describes which group scored higher or lower and what that means for the variable measured.
rubric.example: The gratitude group reported higher life satisfaction. On average, the value was 7.4 for the group that wrote about gratitude and 6.2 for the group that wrote about daily events, and a p value of 0.01 means a difference this large is unlikely to be due to chance.

parts.prompt: Identify at least one ethical guideline applied by the researchers.

rubric.criterion: Identifies an ethical guideline that the summary shows was followed.
rubric.example: Informed consent: participants agreed to take part after being told about the study. (Also acceptable: debriefing; the right to withdraw; approval by an institutional review board.)

parts.prompt: Explain the extent to which the research findings may or may not be generalizable, using specific and relevant evidence from the study.

rubric.criterion: Explains a limit (or strength) of generalizability with reference to the sample.
rubric.example: The sample was 110 adult volunteers from one city, so the findings may not apply to people of other ages, cultures or backgrounds. Because the sample was not randomly selected from a wider population, it may not be representative.

parts.prompt: Explain how at least one of the research findings supports or refutes the researchers' hypothesis.

rubric.criterion: Uses a specific finding from the study as evidence.
rubric.example: The gratitude group reported higher life satisfaction. (7.4 compared with 6.2).

rubric.criterion: Explains how the finding supports the hypothesis, using a psychological concept.
rubric.example: This supports the hypothesis that the type of journal affects subjective well-being. Because subjects were randomly assigned, the difference can be attributed to the type of journal. The finding illustrates positive psychology: practicing gratitude increases subjective well-being.

questions.title: Evidence-based question: Does heavy social media use harm the well-being of teenagers?

parts.prompt: Propose a specific and defensible claim, based in psychological science, that responds to the question.

rubric.criterion: States a claim that answers the question and can be supported by the sources.
rubric.example: Heavy social media use can harm teenagers' well-being, especially when it leads them to compare themselves with others.

parts.prompt: (i) Support your claim using at least one piece of specific and relevant evidence from one of the sources. (ii) Explain how the evidence supports your claim, using a psychological perspective, theory, concept or research finding learned in AP Psychology.

rubric.criterion: Uses specific, relevant evidence from one source and names the source.
rubric.example: In Source B, students who limited social media to 30 minutes a day had lower loneliness scores (38) than students who continued as usual (45).

rubric.criterion: Explains how the evidence supports the claim.
rubric.example: This supports the claim because the study was an experiment with random assignment, so reducing social media use can be said to have caused the lower loneliness. Less time online leaves more time for face-to-face contact, which supports well-being.

rubric.criterion: Correctly applies a psychological concept in the explanation.
rubric.example: The concept must be named and applied correctly, as in the model explanation.

parts.prompt: (i) Support your claim using an additional piece of specific and relevant evidence from a different source. (ii) Explain how this evidence supports your claim, using a different psychological perspective, theory, concept or research finding.

rubric.criterion: Uses specific, relevant evidence from a different source and names the source.
rubric.example: In Source C, many teenagers said they felt worse about themselves after viewing images of peers who seemed more attractive or popular.

rubric.criterion: Explains how the evidence supports the claim.
rubric.example: This supports the claim through upward social comparison and relative deprivation: comparing oneself with people who seem better off lowers self-esteem and satisfaction.

rubric.criterion: Correctly applies a different psychological concept from the one used in part B.
rubric.example: The concept must differ from the one used in part B and be applied correctly.
